headline: PLS rockets +4% on lithium optimism, RBA rate hike talk heats up, and the Iran war hits the six-month mark with no end in sight.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS surged 4.1% today — its best single-day move in a while. A dividend update from the company sparked renewed optimism about lithium sentiment, with some analysts asking whether the sector is finally turning a corner. The broader lithium price outlook remains uncertain (a surplus is still forecast), but today's move suggests investors are starting to re-engage with the beaten-down sector.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: A small gain today, likely supported by modest strength in emerging market equities broadly. No specific catalyst — this one tends to move with global risk appetite and China sentiment.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Edged up slightly today, reflecting a calm, broadly positive ASX session. VDHG holds a mix of Australian and global shares, so it tends to drift with the overall market mood — nothing dramatic either way.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: A tiny gain today. The AI sector ETF is still sitting well below your entry price (down about 13.6% overall), but the daily move was positive. AI sentiment remains strong globally, with big players like OpenAI, Google and Microsoft all in the headlines this week — but market re-rating of AI stocks takes time.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: A small tick upward today, tracking the ASX-listed version of the broad US share market. The underlying US market (S&P 500, NASDAQ) last closed positively; we'll see tonight's US session after 11:30 PM AEST for the next read.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: No live price data available for tonight's US session — markets haven't opened yet (they open ~11:30 PM AEST). Last close was USD $337.71. Recent news is positive: cloud revenue is growing strongly, helping Alphabet hold its own against Microsoft and Amazon. Q2 2026 AI and cloud growth are being cited as key supports for the stock around the $340 level.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: US markets haven't opened yet. Last close was USD $505.06. MSFT is up about 12% since its last earnings report, driven by strong AI revenue growth. A new product called 'Moonshot' is being flagged as a potential additional AI revenue stream. The long-term AI story here remains very much intact.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: US markets haven't opened yet. Last close was USD $233.00. GTA 6 buzz continues — an 'extended look' at new footage was released this week, keeping the hype machine running. Take-Two's long-term value is heavily tied to the GTA 6 launch; this kind of ongoing content drip is a healthy sign for the lead-up.

watch_today.title: PLS: Big day — but hold, don't chase
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals jumped 4.1% today after a dividend update sparked renewed interest. That's a great day for a beaten-down stock (you're still down ~20% overall). The lithium market still has a surplus forecast, so don't read too much into one session. Long-term thesis is intact if you believe in lithium's EV future — sit tight and let it play out.

watch_today.title: GXAI: Still underwater, but AI tailwinds building
watch_today.detail: The Global X AI ETF nudged up 0.18% today but is still down 13.6% from your entry. This week, OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic all issued a joint statement warning about AI cyberattacks — which ironically highlights just how central AI has become. The long-term AI investment case is strong; your position just needs time. No reason to sell.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 hype train keeps rolling
watch_today.detail: Take-Two released an 'extended look' at GTA 6 footage this week, generating massive buzz. This is exactly the kind of pre-launch momentum that builds toward a blockbuster release. Your TTWO position is a long-term bet on this launch — hold and let it play out. US markets open tonight, watch for any reaction.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike incoming? September meeting in focus
watch_today.detail: Multiple major banks have done a U-turn on their RBA forecasts this week — they're now calling for a rate hike in September. The AFR and WSJ are both reporting the RBA is still jittery about inflation, and rising household spending is adding pressure. A rate rise could put a lid on ASX gains and squeeze mortgage holders further. Worth watching closely over the next two weeks.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Strong AI momentum continues
watch_today.detail: Microsoft is up 12% since its last earnings report and a new 'Moonshot' AI product is flagged as a potential new revenue stream. Tonight's US session (opens ~11:30 PM AEST) will be the next real price test. Long-term story is as strong as ever — hold.

watch_today.title: AUD dipped slightly — watch for rate hike impact
watch_today.detail: The Aussie dollar fell 0.43% to USD $0.7164 today. Ironically, rate hike talk usually pushes the AUD UP (higher rates attract foreign money), so watch for the currency to swing around as RBA speculation heats up. A stronger AUD slightly reduces the AUD value of your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO), so it's worth keeping an eye on.

world.summary: The big global stories today: the Iran war hits six months with no resolution in sight, Trump's mail-voting battle heads to the courts, and the IMF forecasts the global economy to crack $150 trillion by 2030.

stories.title: Iran War: Six Months In, No End in Sight
stories.why_it_matters: The conflict between Iran and its adversaries has now ground on for six months, with analysts describing a 'stalemate with no end in sight.' Iran's regime, while battered, remains entrenched and hasn't collapsed as some predicted. The war has reshaped the Middle East's relationship with the US and created clear energy winners and losers — oil-producing nations outside the conflict zone are benefiting from elevated prices, while countries dependent on Middle East supply are paying more. For everyday Australians, this feeds into higher petrol prices and global inflation pressures.

stories.title: Trump's Mail-Voting Order Blocked — Again — and Now Being Appealed
stories.why_it_matters: A federal judge has now twice blocked the Trump administration's executive order that would restrict mail-in voting for the upcoming US midterm elections. The order would have required proof of citizenship for mail ballots. The administration has appealed and the legal battle is heading up the court system fast, with the midterms approaching. This is a significant fight over voting access in the US — the outcome could affect millions of Americans' ability to vote and will shape the political landscape heading into the election.

stories.title: IMF: Global Economy to Hit $150 Trillion by 2030
stories.why_it_matters: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is forecasting the global economy will surpass $150 trillion in size by 2030 — a significant milestone. That's good news for long-term investors: a bigger global economy generally means more corporate earnings, more trade, and more growth for diversified funds like VDHG and VTS. It's a reminder that despite all the short-term noise — wars, rate hikes, inflation — the long-run direction of the global economy is still up.

stories.title: Regional Powers Pushing for Iran War Off-Ramp
stories.why_it_matters: Several regional powers are quietly looking for a way to wind down the Iran conflict, according to reports. Countries in the Middle East are pushing diplomatic back-channels for a ceasefire or negotiated settlement, though no breakthrough has been announced. Markets have largely 'priced in' the stalemate — oil and equities are no longer swinging wildly on every development — but any genuine peace move could shift energy prices significantly and quickly. Worth watching if you hold energy-exposed assets.

politics.summary: The RBA is dominating Australian domestic headlines this week, with growing calls — now including major banks — for a rate hike as early as September. Rising household spending is adding fuel to the fire.

stories.title: Major Banks Flip: Now Calling for RBA Rate Hike in September
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's big banks have done a U-turn and are now predicting the Reserve Bank will lift interest rates at its September meeting. Previously they had been calling for rates to hold or even fall. The trigger: stubbornly high inflation and a surprise jump in household spending data. For mortgage holders, this is a real concern — another rate rise means higher repayments again. For the ASX, rate hikes tend to put downward pressure on growth stocks and property.

stories.title: RBA Still 'Jittery' About Inflation — WSJ
stories.why_it_matters: The Wall Street Journal reports the RBA remains deeply concerned about Australia's inflation outlook, even as the housing market cools. The central bank is caught between a slowing property sector and consumer prices that refuse to come down fast enough. This tension — wanting to cut rates to help housing, but not being able to because inflation is sticky — is likely to keep the RBA in a difficult position for the rest of 2026.

stories.title: Rising Household Spending Heaps Pressure on Labor and RBA
stories.why_it_matters: New data shows Australian households are still spending at a surprisingly strong clip, which is bad news for the inflation fight. The AFR says this puts pressure on both the Albanese government (which wants to be seen as tackling the cost of living) and the RBA, which needs spending to slow before it can ease rates. It's a bit of a Catch-22: the economy is running hotter than the RBA wants, even with rates already elevated.

ai.summary: The biggest AI story this week: the industry's own giants are sounding the alarm on AI-powered cyberattacks, warning companies they have just months to prepare. Separately, Bill Gates has reversed his position on AI regulation.

stories.title: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft & Anthropic Jointly Warn: AI Cyberattacks Are Coming Fast
stories.why_it_matters: Over 100 tech companies — including OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic — have issued a rare joint statement warning that AI-powered cyberattacks are becoming a serious and imminent threat. The statement says companies have just 'months' to prepare their defences, not years. In plain English: hackers are now using AI to launch smarter, faster and more automated attacks. This affects everyday businesses and individuals — think AI-generated phishing emails that are almost indistinguishable from real ones, or automated hacking tools that can breach systems in minutes.

stories.title: Bill Gates Reverses on AI Regulation: Now Backs Oversight
stories.why_it_matters: Bill Gates — who for years opposed heavy AI regulation — has done a public about-face, saying the industry has 'crossed safety lines' and needs oversight. He stopped short of recommending specific policies, but the shift from one of tech's most influential voices is significant. When the person who built Microsoft starts calling for guardrails on AI, it suggests the risks are being taken seriously even at the top of the industry. This could accelerate government regulation globally, including in Australia.

stories.title: Pope Leo's Vatican Weighs In: How Should the Church Regulate AI?
stories.why_it_matters: In an unusual intersection of religion and technology, The Pillar reports that Pope Leo's Vatican is actively considering how to regulate the use of AI within the Catholic Church — and potentially advocate for broader global AI governance. With 1.4 billion Catholics worldwide, the Church's position on AI ethics could carry real moral weight in the global debate. It signals just how far-reaching the AI governance conversation has become — well beyond Silicon Valley boardrooms.

sport.summary: Big NRL Round 26 action across the weekend: Melbourne thumped the Broncos on home turf, the Rabbitohs locked in their finals spot, and Penrith went to the top of the table. AFL finals picture is coming into focus too.

stories.title: Storm Demolish Broncos 46-20 at Suncorp
stories.why_it_matters: Melbourne Storm handed the Broncos a harsh 46-20 defeat at Suncorp Stadium on Thursday night. It was a comprehensive flogging on the Broncos' home ground — not ideal as the season enters finals calculations. Storm continue to look like genuine premiership contenders.

stories.title: Rabbitohs Lock In Finals Berth with Win Over Titans — Latrell Returns
stories.why_it_matters: South Sydney thumped Gold Coast 42-22 at Cbus Super Stadium this afternoon (bad day for the local Gold Coast fans!), securing their spot in the NRL finals. Latrell Mitchell made a timely return for the Rabbitohs and the game featured an emotional tribute to Arrow. With the win, Souths' finals campaign is locked in heading into the last rounds.

stories.title: Panthers Go Top After Beating Bulldogs 24-10 — Despite Injury Concern
stories.why_it_matters: Penrith Panthers beat the Canterbury Bulldogs 24-10 on Friday night to move to the top of the NRL ladder. The Bulldogs had a player sent off in a fiery clash that Fox Sports called a 'brain explosion' moment, all but ending Canterbury's finals hopes. The Panthers are flagging an injury concern coming out of the game — details still emerging — but they're looking ominous at the top of the table heading into finals.

stories.title: AFL Finals: Every Team's Case For (and Against) the Flag
stories.why_it_matters: With the AFL finals just around the corner, both Fox Sports and The Guardian have published detailed breakdowns of all 10 finalists' chances. Carlton's surprisingly strong small-forward is described as being in career-best form — though the Blues' overall case is laid bare as a tough ask. The AFL itself came under fire this week for 'burying' a key announcement rather than giving it proper airtime, drawing criticism from commentators who said the game 'deserves more respect.'
